attempts.name: addpipe24_structural_ripple
attempts.rationale: Frozen-seed data shows the plain 24-bit adder (no partitioning) already dominates all split/carry-select variants in both area and WNS, since partitioning adds extra muxing/select logic without benefit at this bit-width. Rather than repeat that exact netlist, we express the same monolithic adder as an explicit structural full-adder ripple chain (generate loop of XOR/AND/OR gates) instead of relying on Yosys's default '+' inference. This preserves identical sequential/reset/valid semantics but gives the synthesis/mapping tool a more literal, minimal gate-level carry chain, which may map to fewer or smaller standard cells (or at least match the current best) while keeping the short critical path (~2.5ns) that yielded the best WNS in the seed set.

attempts.name: addpipe24_kogge_stone
attempts.rationale: Reward is dominated by WNS (10x weight) vs area (0.001x), so the highest-leverage lever is reducing critical-path delay, not area. The frozen best seed (plain '+') already gets mapped to something reasonably fast (WNS 7.52), while our own explicit ripple-carry attempt forced a 24-deep serial carry chain and got much worse WNS (6.16) despite lower area. To push WNS higher without relying on tool-inferred '+' mapping, this candidate implements an explicit 24-bit Kogge-Stone parallel-prefix adder (log2(24)=5 prefix stages instead of 24 serial full-adder stages). This gives a much shallower carry-propagation critical path than the ripple design, and unlike the tested block-partitioned/carry-select masks (12+12, 8+8+8, etc.) which added serialized mux overhead and *hurt* WNS relative to the unsplit '+' baseline, a full-width prefix tree computes all carries in parallel with O(log n) depth and no extra select-mux stage after summation. This is a structurally distinct design from both prior attempts and should plausibly improve or match WNS versus the best-known 530.936-area design, at a modest area cost that is negligible in the reward formula.

attempts.name: addpipe24_sklansky
attempts.rationale: Frozen data shows plain '+' (WNS 7.51866, area 530.936) already beats every manual partition/carry-select variant, and our own full Kogge-Stone prefix adder essentially matched its WNS (7.51732) but cost ~19 extra area units because every bit recomputes a distinct neighbor at every one of the 5 levels (~n*log2(n) combine nodes). A Sklansky parallel-prefix adder keeps the same theoretical depth (ceil(log2(24))=5 levels, so comparable critical path/WNS) but only the upper half of each group is recombined at each level, reusing one shared reference signal per group instead of a per-bit shifted neighbor. This roughly halves the number of generate/propagate combine cells versus Kogge-Stone while preserving the same logical depth, so it should land near the same WNS at lower area than our Kogge-Stone attempt, potentially improving on the current best proxy_reward point without touching sequential/reset/valid semantics.

attempts.name: addpipe24_cla_block4
attempts.rationale: Prior attempts show WNS is the dominant reward term and hand-built full-width prefix trees (Kogge-Stone/Sklansky) either match baseline delay at higher area or cut area but lose ~0.08ns of WNS, apparently due to wide-fanout combine signals feeding many bits. This candidate uses a classic two-level carry-lookahead structure: 6 blocks of 4 bits each compute local generate/propagate (2-level SOP), block-level carries are obtained directly via a parallel sum-of-products formula across only 6 terms (not a 24-wide prefix tree, avoiding the large per-bit combine-cell count of KS/Sklansky), and each bit's final carry is resolved locally from its block carry-in plus 2 more logic levels. This keeps logical depth comparable to the prefix-tree adders (~5-6 levels) while sharply cutting the total number of combine cells (since only 6 block-level nodes need wide combining instead of 24 bit-level nodes), aiming to land at lower area than both KS (549.8) and baseline (530.9) while preserving WNS closer to baseline than the Sklansky attempt did.

attempts.name: addpipe24_cla_block4_kstree

Kogge-Stone-style prefix trees achieved near-baseline WNS (7.517) because every combine node is a simple 2-input AND/OR regardless of tree position (fan-in/logic depth stays low and uniform). This should shorten the worst-case block-carry path to uniform 2-input combines (matching KS's favorable per-node delay) while keeping the total node count small (tree only spans 6 elements, not 24), aiming to land closer to KS/baseline WNS at area below both KS (549.8) and possibly below cla_block4 (520.8), improving the area/WNS trade on the observed frontier.

attempts.name: addpipe24_han_carlson
attempts.rationale: Prior full Kogge-Stone matched baseline WNS but at +19 area (O(n log n) combine nodes); Sklansky cut area but lost WNS due to high-fanout combine nodes; both flat-SOP and KS-tree block-CLA(4) landed in between without beating baseline reward. A Han-Carlson adder is a well-known sparse hybrid: it first pairwise-combines all 24 bits into 12 group G/P terms (1 level), builds a full Kogge-Stone prefix tree only over that half-size (12-element) reduced array (uniform 2-input combine nodes, low fanout, 4 levels), then does one cheap fix-up level to resolve the remaining half of the carries. This gives roughly half the combine-node count of full 24-bit Kogge-Stone (since the expensive O(n log n) tree only spans n/2 elements) while adding only one extra logic level versus full KS/Sklansky (6 vs 5), which should land at markedly lower area than both KS (549.8) and CLA-block4 variants, at a WNS cost expected to be smaller than Sklansky's (since combine fan-in/fan-out stays uniformly small, unlike Sklansky's later-level wide-fanout reference nodes). This targets a new non-dominated area/WNS point between Sklansky (474.8/7.435) and the tool-inferred baseline (530.9/7.519).

attempts.name: addpipe24_carry_select_1212
attempts.rationale: All previously tried block-partition masks (e.g. 12+12, 8+8+8) split the addition into serially chained sub-adds (carry rippling from low block into high block), which strictly lengthens the critical path versus the monolithic '+' and empirically hurt WNS (7.38 vs 7.52). A true carry-select adder instead precomputes the upper 12-bit sum twice in parallel (assuming cin=0 and cin=1, using the same efficient tool-inferred '+' adder synthesis that produces the best-known baseline), and only adds a single final 2:1 mux stage selecting based on the actual carry out of the lower 12-bit block. This removes the serial dependency that hurt the naive splits: critical path becomes max(low-block delay, up-block delay) + one mux level, instead of low-block + up-block in series. Since the tool's own '+' synthesis for a 24-bit operand already achieves near log-depth timing (matching our best hand-built prefix adder), a 12-bit sub-add is only marginally shallower, but removing the serial carry dependency previously measured to cost ~0.14ns of WNS is a plausible lever to recover or exceed baseline WNS while area grows only modestly from the extra redundant 12-bit adder and mux.

attempts.name: addpipe24_carry_skip4
attempts.rationale: All prior custom adders used full-width prefix/CLA networks that add area but still lose ~0.1-0.17ns of WNS versus the tool-inferred baseline, while pure ripple has the best area but far worse WNS (24-deep serial chain). This design uses a single-level carry-skip structure: six literal 4-bit ripple blocks compute real per-bit sums from the true incoming block carry (guaranteeing bit-exact correctness), while each block also computes a cheap 4-input AND block-propagate signal that muxes the block carry-out directly from the block carry-in when all four bits propagate. Since Pblk=1 mathematically forces the ripple-computed carry-out to equal the carry-in anyway (g_i=0 whenever p_i=1), this mux path is provably value-identical to the ripple result but offers a much shorter alternate physical path for the inter-block carry, letting synthesis bypass slow chains through all-propagate blocks. This should cut the worst-case carry-chain depth roughly in half versus pure ripple (approx block+skip*4+block ~16 stages vs 24) while adding only 6 AND4 + 5 MUX2 cells beyond the ripple baseline, targeting a new non-dominated area/WNS point between the ripple seed (385.168/6.164) and Han-Carlson (469.49/7.345) that the current frontier does not cover.

attempts.name: addpipe24_full_flat_cla
attempts.rationale: Across our own attempts, unstaged/flat sum-of-products carry expressions consistently beat explicitly staged prefix-tree constructions at the same partition granularity (cla_block4 flat SOP: WNS 7.436 beat cla_block4_kstree staged: 7.389; cla_block3_flat: 7.390 beat cla_block3_kstree: 7.353). This suggests forcing an artificial multi-level hierarchy (via named per-stage wires) prevents ABC from finding its own optimal balanced gate network, whereas flat boolean expressions let the optimizer freely rebalance. All previous flat attempts still imposed an artificial block-partition boundary (grouping bits into blocks with a separate block-G/P layer). This candidate removes that boundary entirely: it implements the full 24-bit carry-lookahead recurrence c_i = OR_k[ g_k AND (AND_{m=k+1..i-1} p_m) ] directly via Verilog reduction operators (&, |) over generate-computed constant slices, with no manual staging at all. Reduction operators over static ranges synthesize as balanced multi-input trees by default, giving ABC a single flat boolean network to optimize globally (much like how the native tool-inferred '+' achieves the best measured WNS so far), while avoiding the extra block-boundary logic level that all our partitioned hybrid designs paid for. This is a structurally new experiment (no staged G/P propagation, no fixed radix, no block partition) that could close the residual WNS gap to the baseline while possibly costing less area than full Kogge-Stone (549.8) due to natural term sharing during synthesis.
